meta.name: Air Compressor Troubleshooting Knowledge Base
meta.purpose: Local offline-friendly DB of compressor fault codes, controller tips, and symptom playbooks for field service with Grok.
meta.disclaimer: NOT a substitute for OEM manuals, training, or site safety procedures. Codes vary by software revision and options. Verify against the manual for the exact serial/controller before parts replacement. Always LOTO and depressurize.
how_to_use_with_grok: Ask: "Look up IR Xe code 31" or "Kaeser 0004" or "high temp rotary screw"
Paste a photo of the controller + nameplate (Alt+V on Windows)
Add your own codes: node scripts/add-code.js --interactive  OR edit data/user-codes.json

controllers.name: Elektronikon (Mk IV / Mk5 / Graphic)
controllers.panel_notes: Touch or key panel; shows alarm/warning text and numeric codes depending on generation. Event history under menu. Reset usually requires correcting fault then Reset/Enter.
controllers.access_levels: Operator menus open; service/setup levels require service access (authorized tech / service tool). Do not change regulation setpoints without understanding process demand.
controllers.how_to_read_codes: Note exact on-screen text AND numeric code if present. Capture photo of Event History. Distinguish Warning vs Shutdown.

controllers.name: Xe-90M / Xe-145M
controllers.panel_notes: Graphic controller. Warning flashes; Trip/Alarm solid. Event log lists first-out. Web pages available on some units for logs.
controllers.access_levels: Service levels 0-2 on controller. Level 2 is service. Use only with training. Field Service Tool (FST) for deeper access.
controllers.how_to_read_codes: Warning/Trip codes are numeric (01-55, 200, VSD 100+). Record both code number and full on-screen text.

controllers.name: SIGMA CONTROL 2
controllers.panel_notes: Messages often plain text plus numeric message IDs. Alarm history stored. RFID/service card used for higher access on many units.
controllers.access_levels: Access level 1 operator; level 2 service (service card or authorized code per site policy). Do not reset high-temp trips without finding root cause.
controllers.how_to_read_codes: Photograph display. Note message ID (e.g. 0001 A Direction of rotation) and whether Alarm (A) vs Warning (W).

controllers.name: Supervisor / Supervisor II / WS
controllers.panel_notes: Fault messages on main display line. ? key often shows probable cause. Fault log holds last faults with hours.
controllers.access_levels: Menus for control parameters, maintenance timers, factory setup. Service passwords vary by software/revision — confirm with OEM/manual for your serial.
controllers.how_to_read_codes: Write exact message text. For VSD packages also read drive fault code.

controllers.name: AirSmart / Auto Sentry / Governor
controllers.panel_notes: Major.minor alarm codes (e.g. A1.x airend). Shutdown LED red; Service LED yellow.
controllers.access_levels: Diagnostics menus under controller. Service access per manual / authorized distributor.
controllers.how_to_read_codes: Record major code and minor code, plus advisory text (#301 style on some software).
sources: Gardner Denver AirSmart Controller User Manual

controllers.name: QSI / QGV graphic controller
controllers.panel_notes: Service LED, general alarm LED, automatic operation LED.
controllers.access_levels: Operator vs modify menus; follow instruction manual for service.
controllers.how_to_read_codes: Common text faults: TEMP FAULT, PRES FAULT, HIGH Temp, H.A.P. SHDN, CONT. FAULT, DRYER CONT.

access_tips.summary: Operator can view status and many readings. Parameter/service changes typically require service access for that Elektronikon generation.
tips: Photograph nameplate + controller software version before changes
Use event history for first-out diagnosis
VSD packages: always check drive display, not only Elektronikon text
access_tips.caution: Incorrect parameters can cause trips, overpressure, or damage.

access_tips.summary: Xe controllers expose service levels 0–2. Event log and web pages (where equipped) help diagnosis.
tips: Record Warning and Trip codes
For blower/VSD general alarms, read the drive LCP for the real code
After sensor replacement, verify calibration
access_tips.caution: Only change setpoints with process knowledge.

access_tips.summary: Higher access often requires RFID service card or authorized credentials. Document alarm history before reset.
tips: Never clear high ADT trips without cooling investigation
Note message class Alarm vs Warning
Sigma Air Manager sites: check master controller too
access_tips.caution: Service cards/passwords are controlled for safety and warranty reasons.

access_tips.summary: Supervisor has Status, Control Parameters, Maintenance, Fault Log, Calibration, Factory Setup. Service password methods vary by software — verify against your manual/serial.
tips: Use ? key for probable cause when available
Fault log shows hours stamp — look for patterns
VSD packages: record Supervisor message AND VSD code
access_tips.caution: Password methods vary by software revision.

access_tips.summary: AirSmart uses major.minor codes. Same code can be warning or fault depending on settings (example: power loss P.0).
tips: Always capture full code + plain-language advisory
Shutdown LED vs Service LED tells severity class
Legacy Electra panels may use E0x sensor codes
access_tips.caution: Cross-check software version; advisory numbers differ by revision.

access_tips.topic: Field photo checklist for Grok diagnosis
access_tips.summary: When you ask Grok, attach photos and these details for best results.
tips: Nameplate (brand, model, serial, pressure, HP/kW)
Controller screen showing active alarm
Event/fault history screen
Oil level sight glass
Cooler condition / room ambient
What happened just before the fault
access_tips.caution: LOTO and depressurize before opening pressurized or electrical systems.
